तैस्तैर्भुक्त्वा प्रीतिमांश्च प्रतस्थे ॥२॥
verses.translit:
nirmālyānnaṁ tatra sadyaḥ sametaṁ
dṛṣṭvā harṣād āhnikāny ārabheta |
annaṁ pānaṁ piṣṭakādi prakāmaṁ
tais tair bhuktvā prītimāṁś ca pratasthe ||2||
verses.wbw: nirmālya — освящённую; annam — пищу; tatra — туда; sadyaḥ — только что; sametam — прибывшую; dṛṣṭvā — увидев; harṣāt — радостно; āhnikāni — ежедневные обряды; ārabheta — начал; annam — рис; pānam — питьё; piṣṭaka-ādi — пирожки и прочее; prakāmam — вволю; taiḥ taiḥ — со всеми ними; bhuktvā — вкусив; prītimān — довольный; ca — и; pratasthe — отправился.
notes: Ārabheta — оптатив в значении прошедшего (ради размера).

verses.text: Там Он подобающе отпустил двух министров; они обильно пролили воду из лотосов глаз, и тела их, увы, исхудали; [а прежде] они являли такое рвение! Каков же путь Творца!
verses.orig:
तत्रामात्यौ तेन सम्यग्विसृष्टौ
ताभ्यां भूयो नेत्रपाथोजपाथः ।
तेने क्षामे तत्तनू हन्त ताभ्या-
मुत्साहोऽयं कः प्रकारो विधातुः ॥३॥
verses.translit:
tatrāmātyau tena samyag visṛṣṭau
tābhyāṁ bhūyo netra-pāthoja-pāthaḥ |
tene kṣāme tat-tanū hanta tābhyām
utsāho 'yaṁ kaḥ prakāro vidhātuḥ ||3||
verses.wbw: tatra — там; amātyau — два министра; tena — им; samyak — подобающе; visṛṣṭau — отпущены; tābhyām — ими; bhūyaḥ — обильно; netra — глаз; pāthoja — лотосов; pāthaḥ — вода; tene — излита; kṣāme — исхудавшие; tat — их; tanū — [два] тела; hanta — увы; tābhyām — ими [было проявлено]; utsāhaḥ — рвение; ayam — это; kaḥ — какой; prakāraḥ — способ; vidhātuḥ — Творца.
notes: Министры — Мангараджа и Харичандана (19.94). Хинди: «каков удивительный путь Творца!».

verses.text: Во все края повсюду пришли письменные приказы царя — заранее устроить на каждом месте новое чистое жилище с припасами.
verses.orig:
देशं देशं प्रत्युपेयुः समन्ता-
दाज्ञा राज्ञो लेखपूर्वाः समस्ताः ।
स्थाने स्थाने नव्यनव्यं निशान्तं
सामग्रीभिः कर्त्तुमग्रे पवित्रम् ॥४॥
verses.translit:
deśaṁ deśaṁ pratyupeyuḥ samantād
ājñā rājño lekha-pūrvāḥ samastāḥ |
sthāne sthāne navya-navyaṁ niśāntaṁ
sāmagrībhiḥ karttum agre pavitram ||4||
verses.wbw: deśam deśam — в край за краем; pratyupeyuḥ — пришли; samantāt — повсюду; ājñāḥ — приказы; rājñaḥ — царя; lekha-pūrvāḥ — письменные; samastāḥ — все; sthāne sthāne — на каждом месте; navya-navyam — новейшее; niśāntam — жилище; sāmagrībhiḥ — с припасами; karttum — устроить; agre — заранее; pavitram — чистое.

verses.text: Где бы ни появлялся этот Владыка, там сотни тысяч людей от избытка радости беспрепятственно чтили Его лотосами глаз и прославляли жалобными речами.
verses.orig:
उद्यन्नासीद्यत्र तैरेष नाथो
हर्षोत्कर्षाल्लक्षसंख्यैर्मनुष्यैः ।
निष्प्रत्यूहं तत्र तत्रेक्षणाब्जैः
काकुप्रोक्तैः पूजितः संस्तुतश्च ॥५॥
verses.translit:
udyann āsīd yatra tair eṣa nātho
harṣotkarṣāl lakṣa-saṅkhyair manuṣyaiḥ |
niṣpratyūhaṁ tatra tatrekṣaṇābjaiḥ
kāku-proktaiḥ pūjitaḥ saṁstutaś ca ||5||
verses.wbw: udyan — появляющийся; āsīt — был; yatra — где [бы]; taiḥ — теми; eṣaḥ — этот; nāthaḥ — Владыка; harṣa — радости; utkarṣāt — от избытка; lakṣa — сотнями тысяч; saṅkhyaiḥ — числом; manuṣyaiḥ — людьми; niṣpratyūham — беспрепятственно; tatra tatra — там и там; īkṣaṇa — глаз; abjaiḥ — лотосами; kāku — жалобными; proktaiḥ — речами; pūjitaḥ — почтён; saṁstutaḥ — восславлен; ca — и.

verses.text: «Сегодня или завтра Он непременно придёт сюда!» — так впереди [Него] громко раздавался радостный клич; потом — «Идёт!»; затем — «Эй, эй, пришёл!» — и так снова повсюду.
verses.orig:
अद्य श्वो वा नूनमत्रैष्यतीति
प्रोच्चैरासीदग्रतो हर्षनादः ।
पश्चादायातीति तस्मादुपेतो
भो भोः पश्चादेव सर्वत्र भूयः ॥६॥
verses.translit:
adya śvo vā nūnam atraiṣyatīti
proccair āsīd agrato harṣa-nādaḥ |
paścād āyātīti tasmād upeto
bho bhoḥ paścād eva sarvatra bhūyaḥ ||6||
verses.wbw: adya — сегодня; śvaḥ — завтра; vā — или; nūnam — непременно; atra — сюда; eṣyati — придёт; iti — так; pra-uccaiḥ — громко; āsīt — был; agrataḥ — впереди; harṣa — радости; nādaḥ — клич; paścāt — потом; āyāti — идёт; iti — так; tasmāt — затем; upetaḥ — пришёл; bho bhoḥ — эй, эй!; paścāt eva — после; sarvatra — повсюду; bhūyaḥ — снова.

verses.text: Некоторые почтенные люди там спрашивали: «Где Он, где Кришна-Чайтанья-чандра?» — и тогда те двое указывали им друг на друга: [Пури — на] Господа, [Господь — на] Пури.
verses.orig:
केचित् केचित्तत्र पप्रच्छुरार्य्याः
क्वासौ क्वासौ कृष्णचैतन्यचन्द्रः ।
इत्थं नाथं पूरिणं तं प्रभुं तं
तावन्योन्यं दर्शयामासतुस्तान् ॥७॥
verses.translit:
kecit kecit tatra papracchur āryāḥ
kvāsau kvāsau kṛṣṇa-caitanya-candraḥ |
itthaṁ nāthaṁ pūriṇaṁ taṁ prabhuṁ taṁ
tāv anyonyaṁ darśayāmāsatus tān ||7||
verses.wbw: kecit kecit — некоторые; tatra — там; papracchuḥ — спрашивали; āryāḥ — почтенные; kva asau — где он; kṛṣṇa-caitanya-candraḥ — Кришна-Чайтанья-чандра; ittham — так; nātham — Владыку; pūriṇam — Пури; tam — того; prabhum — Господа; tam — того; tau — оба; anyonyam — друг друга; darśayāmāsatuḥ — указывали; tān — им.
notes: Хинди: «Гаурачандра и Парамананда Пури представлялись желающим их видеть». Шутливая сцена: каждый указывает на другого. В ЧЧ (Мадхья 16) её нет.

verses.text: Когда на рассвете Он приходил к очередной стоянке, все, повинуясь приказу царя, в каждом краю строили чистые дома и в восторге приносили припасы.
verses.orig:
वासं वासं प्रत्युपेते प्रभाते
राज्ञामाज्ञायन्त्रिताः सर्व एव ।
देशे देशे शुद्धगेहानि कृत्वा
सामग्रीश्च प्रोन्मदा आनयन्ति ॥८॥
verses.translit:
vāsaṁ vāsaṁ pratyupete prabhāte
rājñām ājñā-yantritāḥ sarva eva |
deśe deśe śuddha-gehāni kṛtvā
sāmagrīś ca pronmadā ānayanti ||8||
verses.wbw: vāsam vāsam — к каждой стоянке; pratyupete — [когда он] приходил; prabhāte — на рассвете; rājñām — царей; ājñā — приказом; yantritāḥ — понуждаемые; sarve eva — все; deśe deśe — в каждом краю; śuddha — чистые; gehāni — дома; kṛtvā — построив; sāmagrīḥ — припасы; ca — и; pronmadāḥ — в восторге; ānayanti — приносят.
notes: Rājñām — мн. ч. «царей»; возможно, вместо rājño (хинди: «по приказу царя»).

verses.text: Рамананда, дойдя до Бхадры и подобающе отпущенный Им, повернул назад и, страдая от разлуки, отправился в [Шри-]кшетру; а Гауранга пошёл на север.
verses.orig:
रामानन्दो भद्रपर्यन्तमेत्य
प्रत्यावृत्तस्तेन सम्यग्विसृष्टः ।
विच्छेदार्त्तः क्षेत्रमेव प्रतस्थे
गौराङ्गोऽयं सोऽप्युपेयादुदीचीम् ॥९॥
verses.translit:
rāmānando bhadra-paryantam etya
pratyāvṛttas tena samyag visṛṣṭaḥ |
vicchedārttaḥ kṣetram eva pratasthe
gaurāṅgo 'yaṁ so 'py upeyād udīcīm ||9||
verses.wbw: rāmānandaḥ — Рамананда; bhadra-paryantam — до Бхадры; etya — дойдя; pratyāvṛttaḥ — повернул назад; tena — им; samyak — подобающе; visṛṣṭaḥ — отпущенный; viccheda — от разлуки; ārttaḥ — страдающий; kṣetram eva — в [Шри-]кшетру же; pratasthe — отправился; gaurāṅgaḥ ayam — а Гауранга; saḥ api — он; upeyāt — пошёл; udīcīm — на север.
notes: Бхадра — Бхадрак (хинди: «Бхадрешвара»). По ЧЧ (Мадхья 16.151–155) Рамананда провожает Господа до Ремуны и там, прощаясь, падает без чувств.

verses_en.text: Hearing the warbling of the birds — "The night has gone, O Master; leave Your bed!" — He quickly rubbed with His hand His eyes, sealed by sleep, [saying to them,] "Wake up!", and then rose.
verses_en.orig:
रात्रिर्याता नाथ तल्पं जहीही-
त्याकर्ण्य पक्षिणां कूजितानि ।
नेत्रे निद्रामुद्रिते जागृहीति
द्रागाक्षिप्यन् पाणिनाथोदियाय ॥१॥
verses_en.translit:
rātrir yātā nātha talpaṁ jahīhīty
ākarṇya pakṣiṇāṁ kūjitāni |
netre nidrā-mudrite jāgṛhīti
drāg ākṣipyan pāṇinā thodiyāya (pāṇinātha udiyāya) ||1||
verses_en.wbw: rātriḥ — the night; yātā — has gone; nātha — O Master; talpam — the bed; jahīhi — leave; iti — thus; ākarṇya — having heard; pakṣiṇām — of the birds; kūjitāni — the warbling; netre — [His] two eyes; nidrā — by sleep; mudrite — sealed; jāgṛhi — wake up; iti — [saying] thus; drāk — quickly; ākṣipyan — rubbing; pāṇinā — with [His] hand; atha — then; udiyāya — rose.
notes: The metre is śālinī (so the edition: "up to verse 36 — śālinī"). As printed, the second pada has only ten syllables (ākarṇya pakṣiṇāṁ kūjitāni: — — ⏑ — ⏑ — — ⏑ — ⏑): of the four heavy syllables of the opening only three are present, and -ṇya is light; something has dropped out. The printed run pāṇināthodiyāya is to be divided pāṇinā atha udiyāya, "with the hand; then [He] rose"; the division pāṇinā thodiyāya in the transliteration line is merely mechanical.

verses_en.text: Seeing the sanctified food that had just arrived there, He joyfully began His daily rites; and having eaten to His heart's content, with all of them, rice, drink, cakes and the rest, He set out, pleased.
verses_en.orig:
निर्माल्यान्नं तत्र सद्यः समेतं
दृष्ट्वा हर्षादाह्निकान्यारभेत ।
अन्नं पानं पिष्टकादि प्रकामं
तैस्तैर्भुक्त्वा प्रीतिमांश्च प्रतस्थे ॥२॥
verses_en.translit:
nirmālyānnaṁ tatra sadyaḥ sametaṁ
dṛṣṭvā harṣād āhnikāny ārabheta |
annaṁ pānaṁ piṣṭakādi prakāmaṁ
tais tair bhuktvā prītimāṁś ca pratasthe ||2||
verses_en.wbw: nirmālya — sanctified; annam — food; tatra — there; sadyaḥ — just; sametam — arrived; dṛṣṭvā — having seen; harṣāt — joyfully; āhnikāni — the daily rites; ārabheta — began; annam — rice; pānam — drink; piṣṭaka-ādi — cakes and the rest; prakāmam — to [His] heart's content; taiḥ taiḥ — with all of them; bhuktvā — having eaten; prītimān — pleased; ca — and; pratasthe — set out.
notes: The optative ārabheta is used in the sense of the past (for the metre).

verses_en.text: There the two ministers were duly dismissed by Him. They shed abundant water from the lotuses of their eyes, and their bodies — alas! — wasted away; and such zeal [had been shown] by them! What a way the Creator has!
verses_en.orig:
तत्रामात्यौ तेन सम्यग्विसृष्टौ
ताभ्यां भूयो नेत्रपाथोजपाथः ।
तेने क्षामे तत्तनू हन्त ताभ्या-
मुत्साहोऽयं कः प्रकारो विधातुः ॥३॥
verses_en.translit:
tatrāmātyau tena samyag visṛṣṭau
tābhyāṁ bhūyo netra-pāthoja-pāthaḥ |
tene kṣāme tat-tanū hanta tābhyām
utsāho 'yaṁ kaḥ prakāro vidhātuḥ ||3||
verses_en.wbw: tatra — there; amātyau — the two ministers; tena — by Him; samyak — duly; visṛṣṭau — [were] dismissed; tābhyām — by the two; bhūyaḥ — abundantly; netra — of the eyes; pāthoja — of the lotuses; pāthaḥ — the water; tene — was shed; kṣāme — [became] wasted; tat — their; tanū — two bodies; hanta — alas; tābhyām — by the two [had been shown]; utsāhaḥ — zeal; ayam — this; kaḥ — what; prakāraḥ — [is] the way; vidhātuḥ — of the Creator.
notes: The ministers are Mangaraja and Harichandana (19.94).

verses_en.text: To land after land, on every side, came all the king's written orders: at every place a brand-new, clean dwelling was to be made ready in advance, with provisions.
verses_en.orig:
देशं देशं प्रत्युपेयुः समन्ता-
दाज्ञा राज्ञो लेखपूर्वाः समस्ताः ।
स्थाने स्थाने नव्यनव्यं निशान्तं
सामग्रीभिः कर्त्तुमग्रे पवित्रम् ॥४॥
verses_en.translit:
deśaṁ deśaṁ pratyupeyuḥ samantād
ājñā rājño lekha-pūrvāḥ samastāḥ |
sthāne sthāne navya-navyaṁ niśāntaṁ
sāmagrībhiḥ karttum agre pavitram ||4||
verses_en.wbw: deśam deśam — to land after land; pratyupeyuḥ — came; samantāt — on every side; ājñāḥ — the orders; rājñaḥ — of the king; lekha-pūrvāḥ — written; samastāḥ — all; sthāne sthāne — at every place; navya-navyam — brand-new; niśāntam — a dwelling; sāmagrībhiḥ — with provisions; karttum — to make; agre — in advance; pavitram — clean.

verses_en.text: Wherever this Master appeared, there, out of the excess of their joy, people numbering hundreds of thousands worshipped Him without hindrance with the lotuses of their eyes and praised Him with plaintive words.
verses_en.orig:
उद्यन्नासीद्यत्र तैरेष नाथो
हर्षोत्कर्षाल्लक्षसंख्यैर्मनुष्यैः ।
निष्प्रत्यूहं तत्र तत्रेक्षणाब्जैः
काकुप्रोक्तैः पूजितः संस्तुतश्च ॥५॥
verses_en.translit:
udyann āsīd yatra tair eṣa nātho
harṣotkarṣāl lakṣa-saṅkhyair manuṣyaiḥ |
niṣpratyūhaṁ tatra tatrekṣaṇābjaiḥ
kāku-proktaiḥ pūjitaḥ saṁstutaś ca ||5||
verses_en.wbw: udyan — appearing; āsīt — was; yatra — wherever; taiḥ — by those; eṣaḥ — this; nāthaḥ — Master; harṣa — of joy; utkarṣāt — from the excess; lakṣa — in hundreds of thousands; saṅkhyaiḥ — numbering; manuṣyaiḥ — by people; niṣpratyūham — without hindrance; tatra tatra — there; īkṣaṇa — of the eyes; abjaiḥ — with the lotuses; kāku — plaintive; proktaiḥ — with words; pūjitaḥ — [was] worshipped; saṁstutaḥ — praised; ca — and.

verses_en.text: "Today or tomorrow He will surely come here!" — such was the cry of joy that rang out very loudly ahead [of Him]; afterwards, "He is coming!"; then, "Ho, ho! He has come!" — and so again everywhere afterwards.
verses_en.orig:
अद्य श्वो वा नूनमत्रैष्यतीति
प्रोच्चैरासीदग्रतो हर्षनादः ।
पश्चादायातीति तस्मादुपेतो
भो भोः पश्चादेव सर्वत्र भूयः ॥६॥
verses_en.translit:
adya śvo vā nūnam atraiṣyatīti
proccair āsīd agrato harṣa-nādaḥ |
paścād āyātīti tasmād upeto
bho bhoḥ paścād eva sarvatra bhūyaḥ ||6||
verses_en.wbw: adya — today; śvaḥ — tomorrow; vā — or; nūnam — surely; atra — here; eṣyati — He will come; iti — thus; pra-uccaiḥ — very loudly; āsīt — there was; agrataḥ — ahead; harṣa — of joy; nādaḥ — a cry; paścāt — afterwards; āyāti — He is coming; iti — thus; tasmāt — then; upetaḥ — He has come; bho bhoḥ — ho, ho!; paścāt eva — afterwards; sarvatra — everywhere; bhūyaḥ — again.

verses_en.text: Some worthy people there asked: "Where is He, where is He — Krishna-Chaitanya-chandra?" Thereupon those two pointed each other out to them: [Puri showed them] the Master, that Lord, [and the Lord showed them] that Puri.
verses_en.orig:
केचित् केचित्तत्र पप्रच्छुरार्य्याः
क्वासौ क्वासौ कृष्णचैतन्यचन्द्रः ।
इत्थं नाथं पूरिणं तं प्रभुं तं
तावन्योन्यं दर्शयामासतुस्तान् ॥७॥
verses_en.translit:
kecit kecit tatra papracchur āryāḥ
kvāsau kvāsau kṛṣṇa-caitanya-candraḥ |
itthaṁ nāthaṁ pūriṇaṁ taṁ prabhuṁ taṁ
tāv anyonyaṁ darśayāmāsatus tān ||7||
verses_en.wbw: kecit kecit — some; tatra — there; papracchuḥ — asked; āryāḥ — worthy [people]; kva asau — where is He; kṛṣṇa-caitanya-candraḥ — Krishna-Chaitanya-chandra; ittham — thus; nātham — the Master; pūriṇam — Puri; tam — that; prabhum — Lord; tam — that; tau — the two; anyonyam — each other; darśayāmāsatuḥ — pointed out; tān — to them.
notes: A playful scene: each of the two points to the other. Puri is presumably Paramananda Puri, the Lord's companion on this journey (19.6, 12). There is no such scene in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16).

verses_en.text: Whenever He arrived at dawn at one halting place after another, all [the people] in every land, bound by the order of the kings, built clean houses and in rapture brought provisions.
verses_en.orig:
वासं वासं प्रत्युपेते प्रभाते
राज्ञामाज्ञायन्त्रिताः सर्व एव ।
देशे देशे शुद्धगेहानि कृत्वा
सामग्रीश्च प्रोन्मदा आनयन्ति ॥८॥
verses_en.translit:
vāsaṁ vāsaṁ pratyupete prabhāte
rājñām ājñā-yantritāḥ sarva eva |
deśe deśe śuddha-gehāni kṛtvā
sāmagrīś ca pronmadā ānayanti ||8||
verses_en.wbw: vāsam vāsam — at halting place after halting place; pratyupete — when [He] had arrived; prabhāte — at dawn; rājñām — of the kings; ājñā — by the order; yantritāḥ — constrained; sarve eva — all; deśe deśe — in every land; śuddha — clean; gehāni — houses; kṛtvā — having built; sāmagrīḥ — provisions; ca — and; pronmadāḥ — in rapture; ānayanti — bring.
notes: Rājñām is plural, "of the kings"; perhaps it stands for rājño, "of the king".

verses_en.text: Ramananda, having come as far as Bhadra and been duly dismissed by Him, turned back and, afflicted by separation, set out for [Sri] Kshetra; and Gauranga for His part went on to the north.
verses_en.orig:
रामानन्दो भद्रपर्यन्तमेत्य
प्रत्यावृत्तस्तेन सम्यग्विसृष्टः ।
विच्छेदार्त्तः क्षेत्रमेव प्रतस्थे
गौराङ्गोऽयं सोऽप्युपेयादुदीचीम् ॥९॥
verses_en.translit:
rāmānando bhadra-paryantam etya
pratyāvṛttas tena samyag visṛṣṭaḥ |
vicchedārttaḥ kṣetram eva pratasthe
gaurāṅgo 'yaṁ so 'py upeyād udīcīm ||9||
verses_en.wbw: rāmānandaḥ — Ramananda; bhadra-paryantam — as far as Bhadra; etya — having come; pratyāvṛttaḥ — turned back; tena — by Him; samyak — duly; visṛṣṭaḥ — dismissed; viccheda — by separation; ārttaḥ — afflicted; kṣetram eva — to [Sri] Kshetra; pratasthe — set out; gaurāṅgaḥ ayam — and this Gauranga; saḥ api — He for His part; upeyāt — went; udīcīm — to the north.
notes: Bhadra is Bhadraka. According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16.151–155), Ramananda accompanies the Lord as far as Remuna, and there, taking leave, falls unconscious.

chaitanya-chandrodaya.title: Рамананда два года удерживает Господа; уход в Матхуру через Гауду
chaitanya-chandrodaya.summary: Рамананда, не вынося разлуки, своими просьбами два года удерживал Господа, говорившего «сегодня», «завтра»; наконец, получив его согласие, Господь отправляется в Матхуру через Гауду; киннары уверены, что Он вернётся.

verses.text:
Женщина. Чудо, чудо! Так расскажи же и об этом: почему Рамананда воспрепятствовал Ему пойти туда?
Мужчина. Милая! Он так сильно любит Господа, что не выносит разлуки с Ним. Потому, уступая его просьбам, Господь, хоть и желал идти в Матхуру, медлил два года, говоря: «сегодня», «завтра».
Женщина. Значит, отныне Он будет пребывать здесь. Или же пойдёт в Матхуру.
Мужчина. Милая! Теперь, долго уговаривая того самого Рамананду и получив его согласие, Он собрался идти — через Гауду.
Женщина. Благородный супруг! А вернётся ли Он сюда снова?
Мужчина. Конечно.
Женщина. В этом-то и сомнение: ведь Матхура — Его любимое место.
Мужчина. Пусть так, и всё же —

чтобы облегчить тяжкое бремя, взятое на Себя Луной Нилачалы, желающей вызволить всех существ, вплоть до последнего простеца, — этот Пурушоттама снова будет пребывать в Пурушоттаме*.
Женщина. Да, так и будет, так и будет.
За сценой. Бхаттачарья! Как мог Рамананда дать согласие на это дело?
Мужчина. Милая! Слышишь — то самое, о чём я говорил: вот и Гаджапати, удручённый разлукой с Ним, беседует с Сарвабхаумой. Пойдём и мы — послужим Господу, Луне Нилачалы, песнопением. (Оба уходят.)
— Конец вступительной сцены (правешаки) —
notes: Каламбур на puruṣottama: «этот Пурушоттама (Высшая Личность) снова будет пребывать в Пурушоттаме (Пури)». Āpāmaram — «вплоть до самых низких, простецов».

verses_en.text:
Woman. A wonder, a wonder! Then tell me about this too: why did Ramananda prevent Him from going there?
Man. My dear! He loves the Lord so much that he cannot bear separation from Him. Therefore, yielding to his entreaties, the Lord, though He wished to go to Mathura, delayed for two years, saying "today", "tomorrow".
Woman. So from now on He will abide here. Or else He will go to Mathura.
Man. My dear! Now, after long persuading that same Ramananda and obtaining his consent, He has set out to go — by way of Gauda.
Woman. Noble husband! And will He come back here again?
Man. Certainly.
Woman. That is just the doubt: for Mathura is His beloved place.
Man. Be that as it may, still —

to lighten the heavy burden taken up by the Moon of Nilachala, who wishes to deliver all beings, down to the last simpleton, this Purushottama will again abide in Purushottama.*
Woman. Yes, so it will be, so it will be.
Behind the scenes. Bhattacharya! How could Ramananda give his consent to this matter?
Man. My dear! Do you hear — just what I was saying: here is the Gajapati too, grieved by separation from Him, conversing with Sarvabhauma. Let us too go and serve the Lord, the Moon of Nilachala, with song. (Exeunt both.)
verses_en.translit: — End of the introductory scene (praveśaka) —
notes: A pun on puruṣottama: "this Purushottama (the Supreme Person) will again abide in Purushottama (Puri)". Āpāmaram, "down to the lowest, the simple".

chaitanya-chandrodaya.ref: Акт 9, царь, Сарвабхаума и Рамананда, ст. 5–8
chaitanya-chandrodaya.title: Скорбь царя; Рамананда провожает Господа до Бхадраки
chaitanya-chandrodaya.summary: Царь благодарен Рамананде, который вывел Господа на дорогу из столицы, где царь увидел Его, коснулся Его стоп и испил нектар Его речи; с Господом ушли Пури-ишвара, Дамодара, Джагадананда, Гопинатха, Говинда; по царской грамоте на каждой стоянке Ему готовят жильё и угощение. Рамананда, проводив Господа до Бхадраки, плачет; его люди пойдут до самого царства Гауды.

verses.text:
(Входят сидящий на троне Царь и Сарвабхаума.)
Царь. Бхаттачарья, Господь отправился в путь лишь потому, что ослаб узел аркана настойчивых просьб Рамананды.
Сарвабхаума. Какое упорство можно проявить против Владыки? И всё же Он промедлил целых два года.
Царь. Бхаттачарья, Рамананда оказал мне великое благодеяние. Ибо —

он привёл Многомилостивого на дорогу из столицы и устроил так, что я Его увидел;
он даровал мне прикосновение к лотосам Его стоп — недоступное, но сполна приносящее счастье;
он дал мне испить нектар Его речи — милостивой, сладчайшей, пьющейся слухом.
То, чего не удавалось достичь великими усилиями, свершилось вдруг, — и всё же в сердце пустота.
Сарвабхаума. Махараджа! Рамананда — поистине лучший из бхагават. Ибо сказано: «Тот, кто удерживает лотосы стоп Его верёвкой любви, назван первейшим из бхагават» [Бхаг. 11.2.55]. Поэтому Господь в его власти. Потому-то, уступая его просьбе, Господь и оказал тебе такую милость.
Царь. Докуда Рамананда должен Его провожать?
Сарвабхаума. Я слышал — до Бхадраки.
Царь. Сколько человек отправилось с Учителем?
Сарвабхаума. Всего пять-шесть: Пури-ишвара, Дамодара, Джагадананда, Гопинатха, Говинда и другие.
Царь. Увы —

хотя Владыка мира, Господь Синей горы, сияет, восседая на троне, во всём Своём явном высшем величии,
всё же, когда Господь Шри Кришна Чайтанья-дэва вновь уходит на север, — увы, пусты три мира!
Сарвабхаума. Царь! Таков уж образ* любви, свободной от корысти.
Царь. Никто из наших не пошёл следом за Учителем?
Сарвабхаума. Царь, это говорится лишь от любви. Где уж Ему нужда в твоих людях! И всё же до пределов твоих владений кое-кто уже ушёл вперёд с твоей грамотой — он и устроит всё как следует.
notes: В источнике prakāraḥ «образ, способ»; в Kāvyamālā prakāśaḥ «проявление».

verses.text:
Они заранее ставят на каждой стоянке новое жилище, наполняют каждый дом обильными угощениями,
а приставленные к тому люди всюду тщательно всё устраивают*, — и, входя туда, путники стряхивают усталость пешего пути.
А Господь думает лишь, что это дело рук Рамананды.
(Входит привратник.)
Привратник. Государь! Рамананда и другие стоят у ворот.
Царь. Скорее веди их сюда.
Привратник. Как прикажешь. (Выходит и возвращается с ними.)
Царь (почтительно усадив его). Расскажи, докуда ты проводил Господа?
Рамананда. Хотя на каждом шагу мне говорили: «Отсюда, отсюда возвращайся!» — я проводил Его до Бхадраки. Махараджа, трудно оставить путь мирских обязанностей, ибо —
notes: В источнике kṛta-suvacanam uccais tatra tathābhiyuktaiḥ; принято чтение Kāvyamālā kṛta-suracanam uccais tatra tatrābhiyuktaiḥ («всюду тщательно устроенное приставленными»).

verses.text:
даже Его, океан сострадания, спасающий самых жалких, — о Шива, Шива! — я покинул и вернулся только из страха перед тобой.
Ах, почему же не пало там моё тело? Увы, я, чей облик твёрд, как алмазная молния, — я вернулся!
(Проливает слёзы.)*
Сарвабхаума. Рамананда! Ты так твёрд духом — отчего же ты так терзаешься? Таковы уж игры Владыки: Он оставил жителей Враджа и ушёл в Матхуру, оттуда — в Двараку, а оттуда — и ещё куда-то. Как же тамошние переносили разлуку с Ним? Хотя разлука с Ним и невыносима, Он Сам даёт силы её вынести. Так довольно сокрушаться. Тебе следует теперь утешить царя, а не печалить его, выказывая свою печаль.
Царь. Рассказывай.
Рамананда. До пределов ваших владений идут ваши люди. Далее, по дороге, — мои сведущие люди: одни пойдут до самого Гаудского царства, некоторые из них вернутся с не очень далёкого расстояния, а некоторые пойдут ещё дальше.
notes: Ремарка (ity aśrūṇi muñcati) есть только в Kāvyamālā.

chaitanya-chandrodaya.from: *(Входят сидящий на троне Царь и Сарвабх

verses_en.text:
(Enter the King, seated on the throne, and Sarvabhauma.)
King. Bhattacharya, the Lord has set out only because the knot of the noose of Ramananda's insistent entreaties has loosened.
Sarvabhauma. What persistence can one show against the Lord? And still He delayed a whole two years.
King. Bhattacharya, Ramananda has done me a great kindness. For —

he brought the All-merciful One onto the road from the capital and arranged that I should see Him;
he granted me the touch of the lotuses of His feet — inaccessible, yet bringing happiness in full;
he gave me to drink the nectar of His speech — merciful, sweetest, drunk by the ear.
What could not be achieved by great efforts came about suddenly — and still there is emptiness in my heart.
Sarvabhauma. Maharaja! Ramananda is truly the best of Bhagavatas. For it is said: "He who holds the lotuses of His feet with the rope of love is called the foremost of Bhagavatas" [Bhāg. 11.2.55]. Therefore the Lord is in his power. That is why, yielding to his request, the Lord showed you such mercy.
King. How far is Ramananda to accompany Him?
Sarvabhauma. I have heard — as far as Bhadraka.
King. How many people have gone with the Master?
Sarvabhauma. Only five or six: the Puri master, Damodara, Jagadananda, Gopinatha, Govinda and others.
King. Alas —

although the Lord of the world, the Lord of the Blue Mountain, shines, seated on the throne, in all His manifest supreme majesty,
yet when the Lord Sri Krishna Chaitanya-deva goes off again to the north — alas, the three worlds are empty!
Sarvabhauma. King! Such is the way* of love free of self-interest.
King. Did none of our people follow the Master?
Sarvabhauma. King, that is said only out of love. What need has He of your people! And still, as far as the borders of your dominions, some have already gone ahead with your letter — they will arrange everything properly.
notes: The source has prakāraḥ, "way, manner"; the Kāvyamālā prakāśaḥ, "manifestation".

verses_en.text:
At every halting place they set up a new lodging beforehand, fill every house with abundant food,
and the people appointed for it everywhere arrange everything carefully* — and, entering there, the travellers shake off the fatigue of the journey on foot.
And the Lord thinks only that this is Ramananda's doing.
(Enter the doorkeeper.)
Doorkeeper. Sire! Ramananda and others are standing at the gate.
King. Bring them here quickly.
Doorkeeper. As you command. (Goes out and returns with them.)
King (respectfully seating him). Tell me, how far did you accompany the Lord?
Ramananda. Although at every step I was told, "From here, from here go back!", I accompanied Him as far as Bhadraka. Maharaja, it is hard to leave the path of worldly duties, for —
notes: The source has kṛta-suvacanam uccais tatra tathābhiyuktaiḥ; the Kāvyamālā reading kṛta-suracanam uccais tatra tatrābhiyuktaiḥ ("carefully arranged everywhere by those appointed") is adopted.

verses_en.text:
even Him, the ocean of compassion, the saviour of the most wretched — O Shiva, Shiva! — I left and came back only for fear of you.
Ah, why did my body not fall there? Alas, I, whose frame is hard as a diamond thunderbolt — I have come back!
(Sheds tears.)*
Sarvabhauma. Ramananda! You are so firm of spirit — why do you torment yourself so? Such are the Lord's pastimes: He left the people of Vraja and went to Mathura, from there to Dvaraka, and from there somewhere else. How did the people there bear separation from Him? Although separation from Him is unbearable, He Himself gives the strength to bear it. So enough of lamenting. You should now console the King, not sadden him by showing your sadness.
King. Tell it.
Ramananda. As far as the borders of your dominions your people are going. Beyond that, along the road, my knowledgeable people: some will go all the way to the kingdom of Gauda, some of them will return from no great distance, and some will go still further.
notes: The stage direction (ity aśrūṇi muñcati) is found only in the Kāvyamālā.

gaura-stotras.title: Господь в пути с карангой; учит почитать нирмалью
gaura-stotras.summary: Золотой Господь, с кокосовым сосудом у пояса, шествуя поступью молодого слона, Своей любовью к остаткам подношений учит спутников почтению к прасаду.

verses.text: Являя тело, блистающее, как свежее золото, с кокосовым сосудом-карангой, украшающим Его стан, с поступью, прекрасной, как у молодого царя слонов, Он Своей любовью к остаткам подношений наставляет Своих любимых<sup>*</sup>, — да будет весьма милостив к нам тот Бог в облике Чайтаньи.
notes: Karaṅka — сосуд для воды из скорлупы кокоса, атрибут странствующего санньяси (комментарий: Господь в пути, tīrthāya vrajan). Nirmālya — остатки подношений Божеству (гирлянды, прасад): Своей любовью к ним Господь учил спутников почтению к прасаду.

verses_en.text: Revealing a body that shines like fresh gold, with a coconut water-pot, the karanga, adorning His waist, His gait as graceful as a young king of elephants, He instructs His dear ones by His love for the remnants of offerings<sup>*</sup> — may that God in the form of Chaitanya be exceedingly merciful to us.
notes: Karaṅka — a water-pot made of coconut shell, an attribute of a wandering sannyasi (the commentary: the Lord is on pilgrimage, tīrthāya vrajan). Nirmālya — the remnants of offerings to the Deity (garlands, prasada): by His love for them the Lord taught His companions reverence for prasada.

gaura-krishnodaya.title: Выход из Пури в сторону Гауды
gaura-krishnodaya.summary: Простившись с Сарвабхаумой и вайшнавами Уткалы, Господь, жаждая увидеть жителей Гокулы, выходит на бенгальскую дорогу и приходит в Катак, где пляшет перед Сакши-гопалой.

verses.text: Затем, простившись сначала со знающим советы Сарвабхаумой и со всеми вайшнавами Уткалы, Господь, полный нетерпения увидеть жителей Гокулы, отправился по дороге бенгальцев.

С особыми преданными и другими великими [Он пришёл] в обитель владыки земли, подобного огню, и Джанардана [Гаура], радуя там людей, долго, неутомимо плясал перед Тем, кто первый из говорящих правду.<sup>*</sup>
notes: Ст. 2 сверен по скану: niveśam ūrdhvīśitur aurva-tejasaḥ … nanarta dhīraṃ dhuri satya-vādinaḥ. Ūrdhvīśituḥ — вероятно, опечатка вместо ūrvīśituḥ «владыки земли»: речь о Катаке, столице царя, и о Сакши-гопале — «первом из говорящих правду» (ср. 7.44–60), перед которым Господь плясал.

verses_en.text: Then, having first taken leave of Sarvabhauma, wise in counsel, and of all the Vaishnavas of Utkala, the Lord, full of eagerness to see the people of Gokula, set out on the road of the Bengalis.

With special devotees and other great ones [He came] to the abode of the lord of the earth, who is like fire, and Janardana [Gaura], delighting the people there, danced long and tirelessly before Him who is the first of those who speak the truth.<sup>*</sup>
notes: Verse 2 checked against the scan: niveśam ūrdhvīśitur aurva-tejasaḥ … nanarta dhīraṃ dhuri satya-vādinaḥ. Ūrdhvīśituḥ is probably a misprint for ūrvīśituḥ, "of the lord of the earth": the reference is to Cuttack, the king's capital, and to Sakshi-gopala, "the first of those who speak the truth" (cf. 7.44–60), before whom the Lord danced.

gaura-krishnodaya.title: Министры царя; Гададхара и Сарвабхаума отосланы; Ремуна; Рамананда возвращается
gaura-krishnodaya.summary: По велению царя Мангараджа и Харичандана сопровождают Господа; Сарвабхаума и Гададхара, удержанные клятвами, возвращаются в Пури; в Ремуне Господь плачет перед Гопинатхой и отсылает Рамананду, который не смеет ослушаться.

verses.text: Пратапарудра, сильно опечаленный разлукой с Господом, по Его повелению поручил Мангарадже и Харичандане позаботиться обо всём необходимом в пути.
Затем эти двое честных министров, как слуги, радостно служа сыну Шачи, переправили Его через реку, где на волнах играл лунный свет.
Затем Он, почитающий мудрых, провёл ночь в четырёхдверном павильоне на площади; а когда в храмах Шамбху затрубили раковины и Он увидел рассвет, отправился дальше.
Тогда Сарвабхаума и Гададхара, эти двое лучших, остановленные на пути Его клятвами, с трудом обратив [к Нему] сердце, отправились обратно в Пурушоттаму.<sup>*</sup>
notes: ЧЧ Мадхья 16: Гададхара Пандит хотел идти с Господом, нарушив обет кшетра-санньясы, и Господь удержал его клятвой; Сарвабхаума и Рамананда провожали Господа и вернулись.

verses.text:
Успокоив их, Он, сопровождаемый праведниками и окружённый служением других людей, радуя людей мира богатством премы, пришёл в Ремуну, украшение добрых селений.
[с. 64]
В том городе Он увидел Пурушоттаму [Гопинатху], пролил обильные слёзы радости, похитил сердца глядевших праведников и громко ликовал, мудрый, вместе с великими мудрецами.
Радостно проведя ночь в Его дворе среди множества бездомных людей, Он на рассвете, со смехом, отослал сына Бхавананды, хотя тот и противился.
И тот правитель, очень боясь нарушить Его повеление, оставив Господа, которого так трудно увидеть даже ценой величайших усилий, вернулся с войском.

verses_en.text: Prataparudra, deeply saddened by separation from the Lord, at His command charged Mangaraja and Harichandana with providing everything necessary for the journey.
Then these two honest ministers, serving the son of Shachi like servants, joyfully ferried Him across the river, where the moonlight played on the waves.
Then He, who honours the wise, spent the night in a four-doored pavilion in a square; and when the conches sounded in the temples of Shambhu and He saw the dawn, He set out.
Then Sarvabhauma and Gadadhara, those two excellent ones, stopped on the road by His oaths, with difficulty turning their hearts [to Him], set out back to Purushottama.<sup>*</sup>
notes: CC Madhya 16: Gadadhara Pandita wanted to go with the Lord, breaking his vow of kshetra-sannyasa, and the Lord held him back by an oath; Sarvabhauma and Ramananda accompanied the Lord and returned.

verses_en.text:
Having comforted them, He, accompanied by the righteous and surrounded by the service of others, delighting the people of the world with the wealth of prema, came to Remuna, the ornament of good villages.
[p. 64]
In that town He saw Purushottama [Gopinatha], shed abundant tears of joy, stole the hearts of the righteous who watched, and, wise, rejoiced loudly together with great sages.
Having joyfully spent the night in His courtyard among many homeless people, at dawn He laughingly sent back the son of Bhavananda, though he resisted.
And that ruler, much afraid of transgressing His command, leaving the Lord, whom it is so hard to see even at the cost of the greatest efforts, returned with his troops.

advaita-prakasha.title: «Пойду во Вриндаван» — преданные отговаривают: сезон дождей
advaita-prakasha.summary: Шри Кришна Чайтанья тайно говорит преданным, что пойдёт во Вриндаван; они отвечают, что в сезон дождей идти нехорошо, и Он, приняв слово вайшнавов, идёт со Своими на родину.

verses.text: Слава, слава Шри Чайтанье! Слава Ситанатхе! Слава Нитьянанде-Раме вместе с преданными!
Однажды Шри Кришна Чайтанья тайно сказал преданным: «Пойду во Вриндаван».
Преданные ответили: «Сейчас сезон дождей; идти теперь во Враджа-дхаму, как мы видим, нехорошо».
Слово святых вайшнавов — великое божество: нарушив его, губишь всякое благо.
Сказав так, Гаура принял слово преданных и со Своими отправился на родину.

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
One day Sri Krishna Chaitanya secretly told the devotees: "I shall go to Vrindavana."
The devotees replied: "It is now the rainy season; to go to Vraja-dhama now, as we see it, is not good."
The word of saintly Vaishnavas is a great god: by transgressing it one destroys all good.
Having said this, Gaura accepted the devotees' word and set out with His own for His homeland.
He stayed at the Acharya's house in Shantipura; seeing Gaura, the Lord was overcome with love.
Now He roared, now danced wildly, saying again and again: "What good fortune for Me today!"
Of Mother Sita's love one cannot even speak: with the Ganga water of her eyes she bathed Gora's whole body.
Sita's sons were very mighty; of them, on the path of devotion, three were foremost:
Sri Achyuta, Krishna Mishra and Sri Gopaladasa — the Lord rejoiced in the beautiful character of these three.
Their lives were always given to Gaura; seeing Gauranga, they bathed in the nectar of love.
They sang the Name loudly, surpassing the Gandharvas, and at times, intoxicated with love, they roared.
With arms outspread Gaura and Nityananda danced, and all the devotees sang a great sankirtana.
I bathed in the nectar Ganga of seeing Him, and by the good fortune of millions of lives I devoted myself to service.
Mother Sita cooked dishes surpassing nectar and with the devotees served the three Thakuras.
What bliss there was cannot be told: only one who is most fortunate receives such maha-prasada.
Receiving the good news of Sri Gauranga's coming, Mother Shachi came joyfully to Shantipura.
Seeing His mother, Gora prostrated Himself before her, and Shachi-devi took Him in her arms with love.
As Krishna at Kurukshetra in the arms of Yashoda — the same feeling arose in the lotuses of the devotees' hearts.
Who, seeing such a pastime, could remain calm? All hearts were drawn to the shore of the ocean of love.
Then Shachi cooked various dishes, everything Sri Gauranga loved, and bathua greens,
gourd, kalai, sweet rice, cakes and drinks — all surpassing nectar, beyond compare.
Sri Krishna Chaitanya sat down to eat: on the right Nitai, on the left the blessed Sri Advaita.
Mahaprabhu said: "The greens are best of all." Nityananda said: "Something else would be better."
Gaura, laughing, said to Lord Nityananda: "Your love, like the Ganga, flows towards the low."
Nityananda replied: "Your head is turned upwards — how can You see the low, but only the high?"
Then all three Thakuras laughed loudly; only the greatly fortunate grasped even a shadow of the meaning.
Mother kept perfecting her service, and every day there was a festival in the Lord's house.
After some days Sri Chaitanya, the great Lord, set out hastily, saying: "I shall go to Vraja."
In due course He came to the village of Ramakeli and there met Rupa and Sanatana.
Sri Rupa and Sanatana are treasuries of all learning, royal ministers equal in intellect to Brihaspati.
Mahaprabhu showed them great mercy, and, giving up worldly pleasures, both became free from envy.
Sri Chaitanya said: "I shall go to Vrindavana." Rupa and Sanatana privately dissuaded Him.
Both said: "Listen, Mahaprabhu, ocean of mercy: never go (there) with a crowd of people."
At the devotees' word Sri Gauranga turned south and after some days arrived at Shantipura.
With Gaura's coming the bliss of love surged up, and my Lord held a festival of sankirtana.
There Gora met Mother Shachi and, receiving her permission to go to Vraja, set out south (for Puri).
On the way He met Raghunatha Dasa, whose worship amazes the sadhus.
In the waves of fragrance of the wish-fulfilling sandal tree, Gaura, the poison of his worldly enjoyment easily vanished.
Mahaprabhu praised his detachment; that truth I cannot describe.
One day Sri Chaitanya came to Kshetra-dhama and, seeing Jagannatha, melted with the sweetness of love.
Seeing Gaura, the devotees became intoxicated with bliss and held a great festival of the sankirtana of the Name.
After some days Sriman Gaura Vishvambhara firmly resolved to go to Vrindavana.
One day at the end of the night Gora, in a hidden ecstasy of mahabhava, set out for Vraja-dhama.
Leaving the main road, He went by a by-way — through the Jharikhanda forest, to the people's amazement.
He loudly sang the sankirtana of the name of Hari, and on seeing Gaura the beasts gave up their ferocity.
Mahaprabhu said: "Hey, beasts of the forest! Weep, crying 'Krishna,' and all your bonds will be broken."
The command of Bhagavan Himself is surely effective: in love the beasts, crying "Krishna," wept.
In the dense forest a great festival began: by the power of the Name all the beasts and birds were liberated.
What can I say of the greatness of Sri Chaitanya's mercy? By the name of Hari even the immobile beings were liberated in this life.
The pastimes of Sri Krishna Chaitanya are a great ocean of jewels: neither the Four-faced One nor others find their beginning or end.
I, a most insignificant creature, know nothing: for my heart's joy I only briefly enumerate the essence.
The ignorant do not believe this at all; know for certain: it is accessible to the wise.
What to speak of the pastimes of Bhagavan Himself — the divine power of a devotee is seen with one's own eyes only by good fortune.
Mahaprabhu went on, preaching the Name; on the way He made many people Vaishnavas, imparting power to them.
After some days Gaura came to Kashi and bathed in the Ganga at the Manikarnika ghat.
There Tapana Mishra, seeing Sri Gauranga, prostrated himself with the eight limbs of his body in great bliss.
With entreaties he took Him to his house, and Gaurachandra stayed there several days.
Then Gora, beholding Bindu-Madhava, raised His arms and danced wondrously.
Restraining His love, He prostrated Himself and offered manifold praises, like Ananta himself.
Seeing Vishveshvara, Gora was filled with love and only repeated with His lips: "Hari-Hara, Hari-Hara."
Bowing to Shiva, He recited a divine hymn, as Brahma recites the Vedas with his four mouths.
Unearthly is Gora's love, unearthly His form; seeing it, all said: "This is the emperor of sadhakas."
Then Sri Chaitanya, seeing Annapurna, intoxicated with love, called her Paurnamasi.
Now He laughed, now wept, now fainted, now with a roar danced round about.
Seeing this, the people of Kashi were amazed; some said: "This is the incarnation of a god."
Then Mishra took Him to his house and offered Mahaprabhu food with various gifts.
With all his kin he partook of the maha-prasada; there also Gora met Chandrashekhara.
Then Sri Gauranga, beholding the Deity of Adi-Keshava, was lost in pure love.
Thus, having held a festival in Kashi, Gaura Hari went from there to Sri Prayaga.
Seeing the Triveni, He was overcome with love and only called out: "Daughter of Kalinda (Yamuna)!"
"What good fortune — I have seen the Yamuna!" With this cry He plunged into the water.
All day Gora remained under the water of the Yamuna, and in the evening, out of mercy, He surfaced.
Fishermen lifted Him into a boat, and, sitting in the boat, Gora sang the sankirtana of Hari.
All were enchanted by that sweet singing, and Gora, greatly delighted, came out onto the bank.
At the time of the evening arati Shachinandana, seeing Madhava, wept with love.
Raising His arms, Gora roared and said again and again: "Give bhakti! Give bhakti!"
He danced wondrously, as people had never seen; at the manifold love of Gauranga all things moving and unmoving wept.
After a long time Gora restrained His love; seeing the Bhima-ganga, He grew merry.
Then from Sri Prayaga He went along the road to Vrindavana, delivering the souls by the gift of the treasure of love.
In due course Gaura came to the district of Mathura and, overwhelmed by the mood of the gopis, forgot Himself.
"Where is Kanu, where is Kanu, where shall I find Him? Shall I comfort a life scorched by the fire of separation?"
Singing this verse, He became speechless and only wept, repeating: "Where? Where?"
In this state the second watch passed for Gora; at last He began to roll on the ground, so that people were frightened.
After some time, in the ecstasy of His own pastimes, Gora wandered hither and thither looking for Kamsa.
He roared like a lion, slapped His arms, leaped upwards — who can fathom His mind?
Thus various moods flared up in Him, and day and night passed like a single moment.
Then Shachinandana came to the Dhruva-ghat and, remembering the story of Dhruva, wept.
Seeing the crowd of people, He restrained His love, bathed and beheld the Deity.
Then Mahaprabhu came to holy Vrindavana; as soon as He reached Vraja, He fainted with love.
After a long time Sri Gauranga came to Himself, but, repeating only "Here, here," became speechless.
Tirelessly He rolled in the spiritual dust and in mahabhava called out: "Where is My beloved?"
"Where is Kanu, where is Kanu?" He called again and again; day and night He searched for Krishna.
Streams of love flowed ceaselessly from both His eyes; at times, weeping loudly, He wandered from forest to forest.
At times He laughed loudly for a whole watch, at times He roared like a lion — who can fathom the end of it?
Mahaprabhu's mahabhava is inaccessible even to the gods — who has the power to describe it?
Gora wandered along the paths of Vraja and every moment repeated: "Say 'Krishna,' say 'Krishna.'"
At the command of Sri Krishna Chaitanya all things unmoving and moving, like Ananta, cried: "Krishna, Krishna!"
At that time cows and calves surrounded Gaura and began to lick Gaura's body, fragrant with Krishna.
Tasting the nectar Ganga, Gauranga, the cows wept in a great ecstasy of love.
Seeing this, Gora said: "Inconceivable is the nature of Vraja: the people of Vraja have an innate love for Krishna."
Having said this, He placed His lotus hand on the bodies of all, and the cows danced like the gopis of Vraja.
At the dance of the cows and calves Gora's love overflowed, and, crying "hai-hai," He danced like one intoxicated.
Meanwhile Sri Achyutananda, the son of Advaita, was searching for Gora as if mad with love.
Now, crying "Where is Gora?", he roared; now, crying "Sri Gauranga!", he wept uncontrollably.
Now he said: "Where is my Gorachand, my life?" Gauranga learned of the sorrow of His dear devotee.
"Come, come!" — saying this, Gora drew him, and Sita's son, like a yogi, appeared there.
From Shantipura to Vraja is a journey of many days; Achyuta came on the flower-chariot of Gora's command.
Krishna and the devotees of Krishna have inconceivable power: everything is possible, there is nothing astonishing in it.
Seeing Gauranga, Achyuta said loudly: "Hey, Gora, You have taken away my life and come to a distant land!
Leaving the Vraja of devotion, You have come to the Vraja of the gopis. Will You go to the Vraja of devotion, or worship in the love of the gopis?"
Although the Vraja of the gopis is eternally full of bliss, its highest part is the Vraja of devotion.
"For Your sake Sri Yashoda and the other people of Vraja have manifested the Vraja of devotion in Navadvipa.
In what ecstasy have You come to the deserted Vraja of the gopis? To learn this I have come to You."
Sri Gauranga said: "You are the best of bhagavatas: in all beings Sri Krishna appears to you.
In the ecstasy of love you speak so much nonsense! You call empty the place of the eternal pastimes of Radha and Krishna!"
Sri Achyuta replied: "Radha and Krishna united — for the sake of what desire have You now become one body?
The divine form which Ananta and the others have not seen has, by the good fortune of millions of lives, appeared before me.
And yet I called Vrindavana empty — I have committed a great offence; forgive it out of Your goodness."
Gora said: "An eternally perfect devotee of Krishna sees the holy form of Radha and Krishna everywhere.
Krishna regards him as dearer than life and never takes account of his offences.
You are an intimate, eternal devotee of Krishna: in your company love has flared up in Me."
Sri Achyuta said: "Your command is the great Veda; Your most pure mercy makes no distinction between souls.
It is mercy that makes You speak humbly; Your glory is known only to one in whom there is pure devotion.
I am insignificant and know nothing of the true essence; I count only the shelter of Your feet as my great good fortune."
Gora said: "You have deep love for Krishna: by touching your body a soul becomes fortunate."
Having said this, Sri Chaitanya embraced Achyuta, held him tight and in love repeated: "Hari, Hari!"
Sri Achyuta, overcome with love for Gaura, in the mood of a sakhi danced and sang like one intoxicated.
Then Sri Chaitanya remembered Radha-kunda and in the ecstasy of love asked everyone: "Where is Radha-kunda?"
The people of Vraja replied that no one knew; hearing this, Gora fell senseless on the spot.
Seeing Gauranga's mahabhava, Achyuta called the names of Radha and Krishna, and tears flowed from both his eyes.
Hearing the name of Radha, Gora rose with a roar and wept: "Where is Radha-kunda?"
Sri Achyuta said: "Dear Sri Krishna Chaitanya, hear from me the hidden truth about Radha-kunda."
Gora said: "You are an eternal companion of Krishna: the spiritual holy places and sacred sites are known to you."
Sri Achyuta said: "I bow to Your mercy: You always exalt the honour of Your devotees.
You have resolved to reveal to the world two great holy places and to proclaim the omniscience of Your devotee.
The kunda of the Mistress of the kunda has inconceivable power; the same power surely belongs to Shyama-kunda.
Ananta and the other gods find no limit to the two — how should insignificant I know of them?
Know me as a wooden puppet: as You wish, so I dance.
My teacher is Your beloved Gadadhara, Pandita Gosvami, a treasury of love.
My father calls him a part of Sri Radhika: in his company devotion to Krishna is attained.
He mercifully told me these words; I speak them, not knowing whether it is good or bad.
Where Radha, the Mistress of the kunda, eternally abides, that is Sri Radha-kunda — this is the evident proof.
Who knows the limit of the glory of Sri Radha-kunda? She is the very presiding essence of all holy places.
All the holy places, washing away the sins of sinners, themselves bear the heap of those sins;
in the company of saints those sins are destroyed — so say the shrutis: the holiness of the holy places comes from them.
Radha-kunda is the spiritual potency of Krishna, an eternally perfect reality, the shelter of all potencies.
Remembering Sri Radha-kunda destroys all sins; telling of her gives faith in the eternal dharma.
Seeing Sri Kunda gives a sprout of devotion; by a mere touch loving devotion awakens.
Bathing in the waters of the Kunda surely leads to Krishna; whoever leaves the body on her bank obtains the service of Krishna.
Who can list the countless virtues of Sri Kunda? Hear now of some of her secondary virtues.
All the beings living on the bank of the Kunda are perfected souls: hearing the names of Radha and Krishna, they weep.
Merely seeing Sri Kunda heals one's sufferings: the world is forgotten, and jubilation grows in the mind.
Her very water is sweet, like medicine: bathing in it and drinking it prolong life and cure diseases.
Beside Sri Kunda is beautiful Shyama-kunda: like Radha-kunda, it is dear to Krishna and spiritual.
There Sri Nandanandana eternally abides; at the sight of it the form of Krishna is revealed.
Even Sri Ananta does not know its glory: bathing in it and drinking it grant Radha and Krishna."
Having said this, Sri Achyuta bowed to Gaura, and Gora in the ecstasy of love embraced him tightly.
Gora said: "Today I have heard of the glory of Sri Kunda — I consider My body, life and mind blessed."
Having said this, He went on in the ecstasy of mahabhava and came to the almost vanished Radha-kunda.
Sri Krishna Chaitanya said to the Acharya's son: "This is Radha-kunda — look at the signs.
Although this great holy place has almost vanished, at the sight of it the sorrow of the mind has passed.
Why has the jubilation of love suddenly risen so?" Having said this, He cried with a roar: "Radha!"
Hearing the name of Radha, all the beasts and birds wept in the ecstasy of love, like the best devotees of Krishna.
The name of Radha by itself eternally gives rise to bliss — and here it fell from Gaura's lips, full of true love!
Hearing that sound, in whom would love not awaken? In the bliss of love tears flowed from the moving and the unmoving.
Sri Gauranga said: "Look, son of the Acharya: by the name of Radha love has awakened in every soul.
This is the true Radha-kunda, there is no doubt; and the pond adjoining it is Shyama-kunda.
What good fortune — I have seen Sri Kunda! Such is the divine, inconceivable virtue of the company of saints."
Having said this, the all-knowing Lord, intoxicated with the nectar of love, leaped into the water.
Having dipped in Radha-kunda, He crossed to Shyama-kunda, bathed in Shyama-kunda and returned to Radha-kunda.
Having finished His bath, Gora took clay from the Kunda and, overwhelmed with love, smeared it all over His body.
With deep love Gaura Hari prostrated Himself a hundred times and offered the Kunda manifold praises.
Seeing this, Sri Achyuta, intoxicated with love, wandered about roaring: "This is the spiritual Kunda!"
Then Mahaprabhu, in the mood of Radha, the Mistress of the kunda, wept aloud: "Where is the Lord of My life?"
Now stupor, now trembling, now loud laughter, now a roar, now dancing, now humble speech.
The waves of the great ocean of love rose ever higher, and Sri Chaitanya fell senseless to the ground.
Seeing Gauranga's motionless body, Sri Achyuta wept ceaselessly: "Ah, Gaura, my life!"
After some time Sita's son grew a little calmer and in a deep voice began to cry: "Hari, Hari!"
In the third watch Gora came to Himself and broke into dance: "I have found Radha-kunda!"
The two kundas that belong to those Two — He, seeing the terrible age of Kali, mercifully joined and revealed.
Then Gaurachandra, taking Achyuta by the hand, went round the Kunda, reciting the great mantra.
Again and again, hundreds of times, He prostrated Himself; Sri Achyuta in the ecstasy of love bathed in the Kunda.
Hearing his insistent, devoted, humble words, Gora grew a little calmer and sat down under a tree.
Gauranga said: "Achyuta, by the virtue of association with you Radha-kunda has mercifully appeared."
Achyuta replied: "Why do You make me an offender? I eternally abide in the shelter of Your feet.
Age after age You display unearthly pastimes: to deliver the souls You have revealed a hidden holy place.
The hidden love, the hidden Kunda had long been concealed; by Your mercy Radha-kunda has appeared."
Hearing this, Mahaprabhu said: "This is excessive praise. It is his father's dharma — I do not like it.
Krishna alone is the Lord of all, and all others are servants: to see Ishvara in a soul is utter ruin."
Sri Achyuta replied: "By the law of Your pastimes You speak humbly, to conceal the truth about Yourself.
As a cloud cannot hide the sun, so in His manifest pastimes Krishna cannot remain hidden."
Having said this, Sri Achyuta cried out the name of Hari. Gora said: "The Name alone is true — leave other talk."
Sri Achyuta replied: "The Possessor of the Name I have obtained by the good fortune of millions of lives," — and, clasping Gora's feet, he wept.
Then Gora, the ocean of mercy, showed mercy and revealed to him His own perfect form — the Divine Couple.
The form of Sri Krishna, the King of rasas, the most complete; and at His left the form of Radha, mahabhava.
Seeing these two eternal forms, Sri Achyuta, overcome with love, prostrated himself.
He offered manifold praises, composing verses. Gora said: "Why do you praise Me?"
Seeing Gaura again in the form of a sannyasi, Sri Achyuta said: "You have hidden Your form in the body of Radha.
Well: by serving You the service of the Couple is accomplished" — and, having said this, he placed Gaura's lotus feet on his head.
Gora said: "You are an emperor of love for Krishna: wherever you are, Radha and Krishna appear to you."
Having said this, Sri Chaitanya embraced him, and Sri Achyuta broke into dance in the bliss of love.
When the news of the Kunda became known to all the people, they were purified by bathing in it, drinking from it and seeing it.
Then Mahaprabhu went to Govardhana Hill; seeing the hill of the pastimes, He fainted with love.
Coming to Himself, He said: "O best of hills, without Krishna your body has grown old, it seems."
And again He said: "What a wonder I see — ah, ah! The scent of Krishna's body has remained on you.
Come, let Me embrace you and comfort My scorched life; and then I shall go, if I find the Beloved of My life."
Having said this, Sri Chaitanya, with arms outspread, ran to embrace Govardhana Hill.
Now falling, now rising, dancing wherever He was, the Lord went round it, singing the name of Hari.
Unearthly is Gora's love, inconceivable His pastimes: distributing the nectar of mercy, He delivered the souls.
Sri Achyutananda, lost in love, now wept, now danced, now rolled on the ground.
Then Gauranga went round all the forests and holy places; at the sight of the place of the rasa dance His love leaped up.
In mahabhava, imagining that Krishna had disappeared, Gora recited the Gopi-gita and wandered about in tears.
Now He imitated the pastimes of Radha and Krishna, now sang songs, now danced.
The love of Sri Gauranga is an assemblage of great oceans: even Sri Ananta is unable to describe it.
I am a fool, an insignificant worm, I know nothing: I enumerate only the essence from the words of saintly Vaishnavas.
Although Gaura did not wish to leave Vraja, at the wish of the devotees He left it, shedding tears.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.

cc.title: Бхаванипур, Бхуванешвара, Катак; под деревом бакула Пратапарудра в слезах падает к стопам Господа и получает Его объятия
cc.summary: Отпустив жителей Пури, Господь с близкими пришёл в Бхаванипур (туда прибыл Рамананда, Ванинатха прислал прасад), затем в Бхуванешвару и Катак, где видел Гопалу и обедал у брахмана Свапнешвары; Рамананда угостил спутников. Пока Господь спал в саду под деревом бакула, пришёл царь: он то вставал, то падал в поклонах, плакал и молился; Господь, довольный, обнял его, и царь омыл Его тело слезами. Так Господь милостив к Пратапарудре телом, умом и словами и прославился как его спаситель.

verses.text:
(97) Он остановил и отправил домой преданных из Пури, хоть это было не так просто, а затем пришёл в Бхаванипур в окружении Своих близких спутников.
ра̄ма̄нанда а̄ила̄ па̄чхе дола̄йа чад̣ийа̄
Рамананда пришёл следом на паланкин сев
ва̄н̣ӣна̄тха баху праса̄да дила па̄т̣ха̄н̃а̄
Ванинатх много прасада дал прислав
(98) После этого туда прибыл на паланкине Рамананда Рай, а Ванинатх Рай послал Господу множество видов прасада Джаганнатхи.
праса̄да бходжана кари’ татха̄йа рахила̄
прасад вкушение совершив там остался
пра̄тах̣-ка̄ле чали’ прабху ‘бхуванеш́вара’ а̄ила̄
утром идя Чайтанья в Бхуванешвар пришёл
(99) Шри Чайтанья принял прасад и остановился там на ночь. Рано утром Он снова выступил в путь и достиг Бхуванешвара.
‘кат̣аке’ а̄сийа̄ каила ‘гопа̄ла’ дараш́ана
в Катак придя совершил Гопала даршан
свапнеш́вара-випра каила прабхура нимантран̣а
брахман Свапнешвар сделал Чайтанье приглашение
(100) В городе Катаке Он посетил храм Гопала, а брахман по имени Свапнешвар пригласил Его к себе на обед.
ра̄ма̄нанда-ра̄йа саба-ган̣е нимантрила
Рамананда Рай всех спутников пригласил
ба̄хира удйа̄не а̄си, прабху ва̄са̄ каила
в загородный сад придя Чайтанья остановился
(101) Рамананда Рай позвал всех спутников Махапрабху к себе на обед, а Сам Шри Чайтанья остановился в саду за городом.*
бхикш̣а̄ кари’ бакула-тале карила̄ виш́ра̄ма
трапезу совершив под деревом бакула совершил отдых
прата̄парудра-т̣ха̄н̃и ра̄йа карила пайа̄на
к Пратапарудре Рай совершил отправление
(102) Приняв прасадам, Шри Чайтанья уснул под цветущим деревом бакула, а Рамананда Рай отправился к радже Пратапарудре.
ш́уни’ а̄нандита ра̄джа̄ ати-ш́ӣгхра а̄ила̄
услышав обрадованный царь очень быстро пришёл
прабху декхи’ дан̣д̣ават бхӯмете пад̣ила̄
Чайтанью увидев как палка на землю упал
(103) Эта новость о приходе Махапрабху очень обрадовала Пратапарудру, и он поспешил увидеть Шри Чайтанью. Придя в тот сад, он простёрся перед Ним в дандавате.
пунах̣ ут̣хе, пунах̣ пад̣е пран̣айа-вихвала
то встаёт то падает любовью охваченный
стути каре, пулака̄н̇га, пад̣е аш́ру-джала
молитвы возносит с трепещущим телом льются слёзы
(104) Он то вставал, то снова падал в поклоне, охваченный сильной любовью. Со слезами на глазах он возносил молитвы, а его тело трепетало от ликования.
та̄̐ра бхакти декхи’ прабхура туш̣т̣а хаила мана
его преданность увидев Чайтаньи довольным стал ум
ут̣хи’ маха̄прабху та̄̐ре каила̄ а̄лин̇гана
встав Махапрабху его заключил в объятия
(105) Шри Чайтанья был очень доволен его преданностью. Поднявшись, Махапрабху обнял Пратапарудру.
пунах̣ стути кари’ ра̄джа̄ карайе пран̣а̄ма
снова молитвы вознося царь совершает поклоны
прабху-кр̣па̄-аш́руте та̄̐ра деха хаила сна̄на
слезами от милости Чайтаньи его тело стало омытым
(106) Раджа вновь вознёс молитвы и склонился в поклоне, и слёзы, рождённые милостью Господа, омыли всё его тело.*
сустха кари, ра̄ма̄нанда ра̄джа̄ре васа̄ила̄
успокоенным сделав Рамананда царя усадил
ка̄йа-мано-ва̄кйе прабху та̄̐ре кр̣па̄ каила̄
телом, умом и словами Чайтанья ему милость оказал
(107) Затем Рамананда Рай успокоил раджу и усадил его. Так Махапрабху явил Свою милость Пратапарудре посредством Своего тела, ума и слов.
аичхе та̄̐ха̄ре кр̣па̄ каила гаурара̄йа
такую ему милость оказал Гаурарай
‘прата̄парудра-сам̇тра̄та̄’ на̄ма хаила йа̄йа
Спаситель Пратапарудры имя стало благодаря чему
(108) Даровав такую великую милость радже, Шри Чайтанья стал известен как Спаситель Пратапарудры.
ра̄джа-па̄тра-ган̣а каила прабхура вандана
царские министры совершили Чайтанье поклонение
ра̄джа̄ре вида̄йа дила̄ ш́ачӣра нандана
царю прощание дал (отпустил) Шачи сын
(109) Все министры и советники также выразили Шри Чайтанье глубочайшее почтение, а затем сын Шачи отпустил раджу.*
verses.orig:
রামানন্দ আইলা পাছে দোলায় চড়িয়া ৷
বাণীনাথ বহু প্রসাদ দিল পাঠাঞা ॥ ৯৮ ॥
প্রসাদ ভোজন করি’ তথায় রহিলা ৷
প্রাতঃকালে চলি’ প্রভু ‘ভুবনেশ্বর’ আইলা ॥ ৯৯ ॥
‘কটকে’ আসিয়া কৈল ‘গোপাল’ দরশন ৷
স্বপ্নেশ্বর-বিপ্র কৈল প্রভুর নিমন্ত্রণ ॥ ১০০ ॥
রামানন্দ-রায় সব-গণে নিমন্ত্রিল ৷
বাহির উদ্যানে আসি, প্রভু বাসা কৈল ॥ ১০১ ॥
ভিক্ষা করি’ বকুল-তলে করিলা বিশ্রাম ৷
প্রতাপরুদ্র-ঠাঞি রায় করিল পয়ান ॥ ১০২ ॥
শুনি’ আনন্দিত রাজা অতিশীঘ্র আইলা ৷
প্রভু দেখি’ দণ্ডবৎ ভূমেতে পড়িলা ॥ ১০৩ ॥
পুনঃ উঠে, পুনঃ পড়ে প্রণয়-বিহ্বল ৷
স্তুতি করে, পুলকাঙ্গ, পড়ে অশ্রুজল ॥ ১০৪ ॥
তাঁর ভক্তি দেখি’ প্রভুর তুষ্ট হৈল মন ৷
উঠি’ মহাপ্রভু তাঁরে কৈলা আলিঙ্গন ॥ ১০৫ ॥
পুনঃ স্তুতি করি’ রাজা করয়ে প্রণাম ৷
প্রভু-কৃপা-অশ্রুতে তাঁর দেহ হৈল স্নান ॥ ১০৬ ॥
সুস্থ করি, রামানন্দ রাজারে বসাইলা ৷
কায়মনোবাক্যে প্রভু তাঁরে কৃপা কৈলা ॥ ১০৭ ॥
ঐছে তাঁহারে কৃপা কৈল গৌররায় ৷
‘প্রতাপরুদ্র-সংত্রাতা’ নাম হৈল যায় ॥ ১০৮ ॥
রাজ-পাত্রগণ কৈল প্রভুর বন্দন ৷
রাজারে বিদায় দিলা শচীর নন্দন ॥ ১০৯ ॥
notes: У ВЧД — «тогда как Сам Шри Чайтанья остановился на отдых в саду возле храма»; в оригинале — «ба̄хира удйа̄не» («в загородном саду»).

У ВЧД — «…нескончаемых слёз, которыми он омыл тело Шри Чайтаньи»; в оригинале — «прабху-кр̣па̄-аш́руте та̄̐ра деха хаила сна̄на» («слезами от милости Господа омылось его тело»): омыто тело царя, а не Господа. «Анубхашья»: сна̄на — «омытый».

У ВЧД — «а затем Пратапарудра простился с Махапрабху»; в оригинале — «ра̄джа̄ре вида̄йа дила̄ ш́ачӣра нандана» («сын Шачи отпустил царя»). Заголовок издания: «Спутники царя кланяются Господу; царь прощается с Господом».

verses_en.text:
(97) With some effort the Lord made the Oḍiyā devotees turn back, and with His own associates He came to Bhavānīpura.
rāmānanda āilā pāche dolāya caḍiyā
Rāmānanda came behind in a palanquin riding
vāṇīnātha bahu prasāda dila pāṭhāñā
Vāṇīnātha much prasāda gave sending
(98) Rāmānanda came after Him, riding in a palanquin, and Vāṇīnātha sent a great deal of prasāda.
prasāda bhojana kari’ tathāya rahilā
prasāda eating having done there He stayed
prātaḥ-kāle cali’ prabhu ‘bhuvaneśvara’ āilā
in the morning going the Lord to Bhuvaneśvara came
(99) After taking the prasāda He stayed there, and setting out in the morning, the Lord came to Bhuvaneśvara.
‘kaṭake’ āsiyā kaila ‘gopāla’ daraśana
to Kaṭaka coming He made of Gopāla darśana
svapneśvara-vipra kaila prabhura nimantraṇa
the brāhmaṇa Svapneśvara made of the Lord invitation
(100) Coming to Kaṭaka, He had darśana of Gopāla, and the brāhmaṇa Svapneśvara invited the Lord for a meal.
rāmānanda-rāya saba-gaṇe nimantrila
Rāmānanda Rāya all the associates invited
bāhira udyāne āsi, prabhu vāsā kaila
in an outer garden coming the Lord residence made
(101) Rāmānanda Rāya invited all the associates, and the Lord came to a garden outside the town and stayed there.
bhikṣā kari’ bakula-tale karilā viśrāma
the meal having taken under a bakula tree made rest
pratāparudra-ṭhāñi rāya karila payāna
to Pratāparudra Rāya made departure
(102) After His meal He rested under a bakula tree, and Rāmānanda Rāya went to Pratāparudra.
śuni’ ānandita rājā ati-śīghra āilā
hearing delighted the king very quickly came
prabhu dekhi’ daṇḍavat bhūmete paḍilā
the Lord seeing like a rod on the ground fell
(103) Delighted at the news, the king came at once, and seeing the Lord, he fell flat on the ground like a rod.
punaḥ uṭhe, punaḥ paḍe praṇaya-vihvala
again he rises again he falls overwhelmed by love
stuti kare, pulakāṅga, paḍe aśru-jala
prayers he offers with hair standing on end fall tears
(104) Overwhelmed by love, he rose and fell again and again; he offered prayers, the hair of his body stood on end, and tears flowed from his eyes.
tām̐ra bhakti dekhi’ prabhura tuṣṭa haila mana
his devotion seeing of the Lord pleased became the mind
uṭhi’ mahāprabhu tām̐re kailā āliṅgana
rising Mahāprabhu him made embrace
(105) Seeing his devotion, the Lord was pleased at heart. Mahāprabhu rose and embraced him.
punaḥ stuti kari’ rājā karaye praṇāma
again prayers offering the king makes obeisance
prabhu-kṛpā-aśrute tām̐ra deha haila snāna
in the tears of the Lord’s mercy his body became bathed
(106) Again the king offered prayers and bowed down, and his body was bathed in tears of the Lord’s mercy.*
sustha kari, rāmānanda rājāre vasāilā
calm making Rāmānanda the king seated
kāya-mano-vākye prabhu tām̐re kṛpā kailā
in body, mind and words the Lord to him mercy showed
(107) Rāmānanda calmed the king and seated him, and the Lord showed him mercy in body, mind and words.
aiche tām̐hāre kṛpā kaila gaurarāya
such to him mercy showed Gaurarāya
‘pratāparudra-saṁtrātā’ nāma haila yāya
the Saviour of Pratāparudra the name became by which
(108) Gaurarāya showed him such mercy that He came to be called “the Saviour of Pratāparudra.”
rāja-pātra-gaṇa kaila prabhura vandana
the royal ministers made of the Lord homage
rājāre vidāya dilā śacīra nandana
to the king leave gave of Śacī the son
(109) The king’s ministers paid homage to the Lord, and Śacī’s son gave the king leave to go.

প্রাতঃকালে চলি’ প্রভু ‘ভুবনেশ্বর’ আইলা ॥ ৯৯ ॥

বাহির উদ্যানে আসি, প্রভু বাসা কৈল ॥ ১০১ ॥
ভিক্ষা করি’ বকুল-তলে করিলা বিশ্রাম ৷
প্রতাপরুদ্র-ঠাঞি রায় করিল পয়ান ॥ ১০২ ॥
শুনি’ আনন্দিত রাজা অতিশীঘ্র আইলা ৷
প্রভু দেখি’ দণ্ডবৎ ভূমেতে পড়িলা ॥ ১০৩ ॥
পুনঃ উঠে, পুনঃ পড়ে প্রণয়-বিহ্বল ৷
